verdict_rule: Each claim is split into the sub-claims its sentence makes. A sub-claim is CLEARED only when every evidence test passes; any failed test or any statement with no accessible evidence makes it EXCLUDED (docs/43 :1945, 'each cleared or excluded'). A 'narrowed' form records a weaker sentence the evidence does support, with its own binary verdict; it never changes the verdict of the sub-claim as written.

claims.assertion: The PbO2 considered for the tier is beta-PbO2 (plattnerite), the rutile-type polymorph.

subclaims.text: β-PbO₂ (plattnerite) is a rutile-type PbO₂ polymorph recorded at ambient pressure.

claims.polymorphism_note: alpha-PbO2 (scrutinyite, Pbcn) is a second PbO2 polymorph recorded without a stated high pressure. The Pnma-type and fluorite-type records carry GPa-range pressures (values in the COD table).

checks.reason: An oxygen-deficiency statement, not a structure type; the COD records parsed here carry full O occupancy and no accessible primary text on PbO2-x stoichiometry was read.

claims.fragment: mp-996 *is* P4₂/mnm (sg 136) with corner- and edge-sharing OsO₆ octahedra, i.e. rutile; "Hydrophilite" is an MP auto-classification artefact
claims.assertion: OsO2 (MP mp-996) is rutile-type P4_2/mnm; the MP 'Hydrophilite' label does not make it CaCl2-type.

subclaims.text: MP mp-996 (OsO₂) is P4₂/mnm (sg 136) with corner- and edge-sharing OsO₆ octahedra, i.e. rutile-type; the two OsO₂ entries in this COD census are also rutile-type.
The MP label "Hydrophilite" on mp-996 is a classification artefact: hydrophilite is the CaCl₂-type (Pnnm) mineral, which cannot coexist with sg 136.

claims.polymorphism_note: COD holds no second OsO2 polymorph; MP lists a Pa-3 entry above the hull (value in the MP table).

claims.assertion: SnO2 (cassiterite) is the ambient rutile-type P4_2/mnm phase; Sn(IV) is d10.

subclaims.text: Sn in SnO₂ (formally Sn⁴⁺) is d¹⁰.

claims.polymorphism_note: Every parsed COD SnO2 entry is rutile-type. MP lists CaCl2-type (Pnnm), alpha-PbO2-type (Pbcn) and other SnO2 entries close above the rutile ground state (values in the MP table); COD holds none of them.

claims.fragment: rutile-type GeO₂ *is* the ambient-stable polymorph and converts to quartz-type above ~1035 °C; stishovite is the high-pressure case
claims.assertion: Rutile-type GeO2 (argutite) is the ambient-stable polymorph; quartz-type GeO2 is the high-temperature form; stishovite is the high-pressure case.

subclaims.text: Rutile-type GeO₂ (argutite) is a GeO₂ polymorph recorded at ambient pressure.
Rutile-type is the thermodynamically stable GeO₂ polymorph at ambient conditions.

checks.reason: A phase-equilibrium statement; no measured GeO2 phase-equilibrium text was read, and quartz-type GeO2 is also recorded at ambient pressure, so the existence of records does not decide stability.

narrowed.text: Rutile-type is the lowest-energy GeO₂ entry in the Materials Project (DFT, 0 K).

subclaims.text: GeO₂ converts from rutile-type to quartz-type above ~1035 °C.

checks.reason: A transition temperature; no accessible primary text giving it was read, and crystal-structure records do not carry it.

subclaims.text: Stishovite (rutile-type SiO₂) is the high-pressure case.

checks.reason: A statement about SiO2, outside the five F8 formulas; no SiO2 record or text was read.

claims.polymorphism_note: Rutile-type (argutite) and alpha-quartz-type GeO2 are both recorded without a stated high pressure. The CaCl2-type and alpha-PbO2-type records carry GPa-range pressures or are ab initio.

claims.assertion: Rutile-type is an ambient polymorph of GeO2, so GeO2 is not excluded on phase grounds (the A7.6 item 5 correction of record).

subclaims.text: Rutile-type GeO₂ is an ambient GeO₂ polymorph (a real phase, not a model phase).

claims.polymorphism_note: 'Its ambient polymorph' reads as unique; alpha-quartz-type GeO2 is also recorded without a stated high pressure. Read as 'the stable one', the sentence carries sub-claim GeO2-rutile-type-is-ambient-stable, which is EXCLUDED.

claims.fragment: **PtO₂** — ground state is not rutile (α = CdI₂-type hexagonal, β = CaCl₂-type orthorhombic per the physics critic; **UNVERIFIED**, check one ICSD/MP record)
claims.assertion: PtO2's ground state is not rutile; alpha-PtO2 is CdI2-type and beta-PtO2 is CaCl2-type orthorhombic.

subclaims.text: The PtO₂ ground state is not rutile-type.
A CdI₂-type hexagonal PtO₂ phase is recorded.
The CdI₂-type hexagonal phase is α-PtO₂.

claims.polymorphism_note: COD records a CdI2-type P-3m1 PtO2 cell and a P6_3mc hexagonal cell from the same 1971 source (neither record names a Greek-letter polymorph), and two CaCl2-type (Pnnm) beta-PtO2 refinements whose titles describe high-oxygen-pressure and high-pressure syntheses. MP holds a rutile-type PtO2 entry above the hull that carries an ICSD cross-reference, so a rutile-type record exists in ICSD although none is in COD.

claims.fragment: The union is 14 real rutile/rutile-like MO2.
claims.assertion: PtO2, SnO2 and OsO2 belong to a union of 'real rutile/rutile-like MO2'.

subclaims.text: PtO₂ is a real rutile-like dioxide (through its CaCl₂-type phase, an orthorhombic rutile derivative).
SnO₂ is a real rutile-type dioxide.
OsO₂ is a real rutile-type dioxide.

claims.polymorphism_note: Holds for PtO2 only as 'rutile-like' (CaCl2-type is an orthorhombic derivative of rutile); rutile PtO2(110) as computed in the cited screens is a model phase. The union's other members (including TaO2) are outside the five formulas.
